drivers.variant_notes: Oliver's free-play set uses the two 4 KiB U2/U6 loader. The archive readme specifies 2732 hardware and S17–19 on for free play.
Free Play+ with replacement 2 KiB 2716 images at U2 and U6 in the stock BY17 memory map. Variant-specific behavior has no retained native run.

drivers.description: Mata Hari (Free Play and MODified rules)
drivers.variant_notes: Quench V22, two 4 KiB images in the BY35 address map on a suitably configured MPU. DIP 19 off retains six player digits and virtual millions.

drivers.description: Mata Hari (Free Play and MODified rules, 7-digit)
drivers.variant_notes: Same V22 ROM bytes and 4 KiB MPU addressing as matahard. DIP 19 on and a separate millions-digit strobe to all four aftermarket seven-digit player displays. Stock credits and match/ball fields remain two digits each.
Factory six-digit set, 2 KiB U2 and U6 images in the BY17 map.
Oliver revision 7 uses two 2732 program EPROMs, with new rules, a skill shot and DIP 25/26 free play.

physical.notes: Cabinet plumb bob and roll cage (A4J3-2/-15) parallel the playfield tilt contact at the listed A4J2 pair. Its precise under-playfield location is unresolved.
Two parallel contacts are drawn. Manual page 2 identifies one factory door contact and optional extra cabinet contacts. Page 17 prints SLAM (2).
The factory callout locates this switch at HitTarget.Target9. Both VPX versions assign 17 to HitTarget.Target6, reversing the bank.

mechanisms.behavior: One ball rests on the outhole wire below the flippers. The ROM counts and serves it to the right shooter alley. Release the switch when the ball clears the contact. The plunger is manual.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and shooter feed

mechanisms.behavior: The cup holds one ball and the closed contact signals occupancy. The ROM awards saucer scoring and fires the kicker. Release the contact when the ball actually exits.
mechanisms.label: Top-centre saucer

mechanisms.behavior: Four individual D, C, B, A switches bottom to top. Contacts hold closed as their targets latch down. A shared reset drive returns all four targets up and opens those contacts. The stock probe reset both banks after all eight targets fell.
mechanisms.label: Left four-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Four individual D, C, B, A switches bottom to top. Contacts hold closed as their targets latch down. A shared reset drive returns all four targets up and opens those contacts. The stock probe reset both banks after all eight targets fell.
mechanisms.label: Right four-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Two parallel 10-point rebound contacts behind the banks. Either momentary closure gives the same matrix address. The upper VPX sling events represent the contacts.
mechanisms.label: Upper target-area rebound contacts

mechanisms.behavior: The ball briefly closes the contact. With play enabled the ROM pulses this assembly's coil. The conversion uses native simulated rebound geometry.
mechanisms.label: Bottom left thumper bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The ball briefly closes the contact. With play enabled the ROM pulses this assembly's coil. The conversion uses native simulated rebound geometry.
mechanisms.label: Top left thumper bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The ball briefly closes the contact. With play enabled the ROM pulses this assembly's coil. The conversion uses native simulated rebound geometry.
mechanisms.label: Top right thumper bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The ball briefly closes the contact. With play enabled the ROM pulses this assembly's coil. The conversion uses native simulated rebound geometry.
mechanisms.label: Bottom right thumper bumper

mechanisms.behavior: The ball briefly closes the contact. With play enabled the ROM pulses this assembly's coil. The conversion uses native simulated rebound geometry.
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The ball briefly closes the contact. With play enabled the ROM pulses this assembly's coil. The conversion uses native simulated rebound geometry.
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet button and K1 contact energize the dual-winding assembly. Local EOS opens at end of stroke and the return spring lowers the flipper at release. PinMAME publishes one held enabled-button pair for the assembly.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet button and K1 contact energize the dual-winding assembly. Local EOS opens at end of stroke and the return spring lowers the flipper at release. PinMAME publishes one held enabled-button pair for the assembly.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: One backbox relay has two contacts, one for each local flipper circuit. The ROM asserts its driver when play is enabled and drops it on tilt.
mechanisms.label: K1 flipper enable

mechanisms.behavior: Passive ball gate in the upper right shooter arch. It lets a launched ball enter the upper playfield and restricts return to the shooter alley.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane ball gate

mechanisms.behavior: Four switched chime coils provide scoring and tunes. The driver declares no sound board.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet chime assembly

mechanisms.behavior: The backbox knocker is a momentary coil with a physical strike. It is separate from the four chimes.
mechanisms.label: Replay knocker

mechanisms.behavior: One continuous lockout coil serves the coin door, which carries right and left chutes and a provision for a centre chute. The chute contacts report accepted coins independently.
mechanisms.label: Coin door lockout

physical.notes: Assembly drive. A6 shows two parallel coil symbols on this line. The parts list and retained underside view do not establish two fitted coils per bank.
Assembly drive. A6 shows two parallel coil symbols on this line. The parts list and retained underside view do not establish two fitted coils per bank.
No factory load on this line. A pulse is observed during fresh boot and its ROM purpose is unverified.

Core mirror of the same enabled button held state. It does not measure a second actuator or winding.
PinMAME's synthesized active state represents the flipper assembly. K1 enables the physical button circuit. A local EOS contact switches the winding circuit.

A5/A6 specify two bulbs, one for each B indicator. L36a models the top insert. I36b and l36c overlap the side insert. Confirm both underside socket centers.

Factory right lower cap. The stock three-ball probe published 41 and 57 together on the first A/B completion. Drive the right cap from 41. The retained VPX builds and the corpus v2.0.0 drive both caps from 41.
Two overlapping lights paint one 3X potential arrow. The socket center is unresolved.
Two lights paint one shoot-again insert. The socket center is unresolved.
Two lights paint one 3X multiplier insert. The socket center is unresolved.
A6 misprints A5J1-1. The A5 decoder and A5 connector list agree on J3-1.
A5/A6 specify two bulbs, one for each A indicator. L52a models the top insert. I52b and I52c overlap the side insert. Confirm both underside socket centers.

Factory left lower cap. The stock three-ball probe published 57 alongside 41 on the first A/B completion. Drive the left cap from 57. The retained BumpLight1 follows 41, as does the left cap in corpus v2.0.0. Upper-right BumpLight3 belongs to VPX GI.
Two overlapping lights paint one 2X potential arrow. The socket center is unresolved.
A6 labels J3-13 CREDIT INDICATOR. The mounted apron lens is on the playfield assembly.
